name: Question 11
problem: The curve $C$ is the intersection of a surface $S,$ defined by $z=f(x,y),$ with the plane $y=-3.$ Given that the point $P(2,-3,3)$ lies on $C$, and that ${f}_{x}=6(x-1)$, which of the following gives a tangent vector to $C$ at $P?$
worked_solution:
The curve $C$ is the intersection of the surface with the plane $y=-3.$ Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve $C$ at the point $P$ will be given by the partial derivative ${f}_{x}(2,-3).$ 

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ at $(2,-3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(2,-3) & =6(2-1)=6\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we use the point-slope form of a straight line:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-f(2,-3) & ={f}_{x}(2,-3)(x-2) \\ z-3 & =6(x-2) \\ z-3 & =6x-12 \\ z & =6x-9\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangent line to the curve $C$ at $P(1,1,0)$ can be given as the intersection of two planes:

$$
{\begin{aligned}y=-3 \\ z=6x-9\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that:

- For the plane $y=-3,$ a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{1}=⟨0,1,0⟩.$

- For the plane $z=6x-9$ (or $6x-z-9=0$), a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{2}=⟨6,0,-1⟩.$

Finally, to find a direction vector for the tangent line, we calculate the cross product of these normal vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{n}_{1}\times {n}_{2} & =⟨0,1,0⟩\times ⟨6,0,-1⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 6 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-i-6\,k \\  & =⟨-1,0,-6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since $⟨-1,0,-6⟩$ is parallel to the tangent line, then $-⟨-1,0,-6⟩=⟨1,0,6⟩$ is also parallel to it.

Question 11
?

The curve C is the intersection of a surface S, defined by z=f(x,y), with the plane y=−3. Given that the point P(2,−3,3) lies on C, and that fx=6(x−1), which of the following gives a tangent vector to C at P?

a
⟨2,0,−3⟩
b
⟨1,1,−2⟩
c
⟨1,0,6⟩
d
⟨−1,1,2⟩
e
⟨2,0,3⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The curve C is the intersection of the surface with the plane y=−3. Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve C at the point P will be given by the partial derivative fx(2,−3).

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative fx(x,y) at (2,−3):

fx(2,−3)=6(2−1)=6

Now, we use the point-slope form of a straight line:

z−f(2,−3)=fx(2,−3)(x−2)z−3=6(x−2)z−3=6x−12z=6x−9

Therefore, the tangent line to the curve C at P(1,1,0) can be given as the intersection of two planes: {y=−3z=6x−9

Next, notice that:

  • For the plane y=−3, a normal vector to the plane is n1=⟨0,1,0⟩.

  • For the plane z=6x−9 (or 6x−z−9=0), a normal vector to the plane is n2=⟨6,0,−1⟩.

Finally, to find a direction vector for the tangent line, we calculate the cross product of these normal vectors:

n1×n2=⟨0,1,0⟩×⟨6,0,−1⟩=ijk01060−1=−i−6k=⟨−1,0,−6⟩

Finally, since ⟨−1,0,−6⟩ is parallel to the tangent line, then −⟨−1,0,−6⟩=⟨1,0,6⟩ is also parallel to it.
